# Uppalavaṇṇātherīgāthā (Thig 11.1)

**ID:** Thig 11.1
**Section:** Therīgāthā (thig)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Uppalavaṇṇātherīgāthā
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0509m.mul10.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The biographical framing in Dhammapāla's commentary (*Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, Thī-a XI.1) embeds these stanzas within an extensive narrative of her renunciation involving incest, incorporating material from the *Apadāna* (*Thi-Ap* 19) [Silk 2009; Collett 2014]. This Theravāda exegetical account shares thematic connections with, yet differs significantly from, the elaborate tale of Utpalavarṇā found in the *Vinayavibhaṅga* of the *Mūlasarvāstivāda-vinaya* [Silk 2009; Buswell & Lopez 2014; Collett 2014]. In contrast to these narrative traditions, the canonical verses themselves focus strictly on her confrontation with Māra and her spiritual mastery [Collett 2014].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Passage-level parallels: SN 5.5 Uppalavaṇṇāsutta
- Mentioned in: Thi-Ap 19 Uppalavaṇṇātherīapadāna

**Sources**

- [Buswell & Lopez 2014] Robert E. Buswell Jr. and Donald S. Lopez Jr., Princeton Dictionary of Buddhism (2014) — Information on Uppalavaṇṇā's Therīgāthā verses and commentary versus Sanskrit Vinayavibhaṅga accounts.
- [Silk 2009] Jonathan A. Silk, Riven by Lust: Incest and Schism in Indian Buddhist Legend and Historiography (2009) — Comparison between the Therīgāthā commentary narrative and the Mūlasarvāstivāda-vinaya story.
- [Bingenheimer] Marcus Bingenheimer, Studies in Agama Literature: With Special Reference to the Shorter Chinese Saṁyuktāgama — Listing of Chinese parallels to Uppalavaṇṇātherīgāthā in Za ahan and Bieyi za ahan.
- [Collett 2014] Alice Collett (ed.), Women in Early Indian Buddhism: Comparative Textual Studies (2014) — Details on the chariot verse, commentary citation (Thī-a XI.1), and comparison with Apadāna and Bhikkhunī Saṁyutta.
